subsystems.name: Unit module
subsystems.role: the repeating building block: a small self-contained robot that can act alone or lock together with others.

subsystems.name: Docking and connection system
subsystems.role: lets modules grip each other rigidly and pass power and data across the joint.

subsystems.name: Actuation and locomotion
subsystems.role: how a single module moves, and how an assembled structure crawls, rolls or walks.

subsystems.name: Distributed control and communication
subsystems.role: no central brain: modules sense neighbours and agree locally on what shape to form.

subsystems.name: Power and energy management
subsystems.role: keeps hundreds or thousands of small batteries charged and shares power through the structure.

subsystems.name: Reconfiguration planner
subsystems.role: decides which shape is needed for a job and which module moves where — the part that today exists only in simulation.

buildSteps.title: Fix the module specification
buildSteps.detail: Pick the trade-off between module size, force it can exert, power it can carry and cost. Smaller modules give finer shapes but weaker joints.

buildSteps.title: Fabricate the module
buildSteps.detail: Assemble microcontroller boards, actuator or flywheel, battery and housing into a unit typically a few centimetres across.

buildSteps.title: Make the docking face
buildSteps.detail: Machine alignment cones and a latch with electrical contacts, then cycle it thousands of times to check it still engages reliably.

buildSteps.title: Write the firmware
buildSteps.detail: Each module gets code for sensing its neighbours, aligning itself, latching on, and reporting its position in the structure.

buildSteps.title: Write the swarm controller
buildSteps.detail: Local rules let modules self-assemble into a target shape without any unit knowing the whole plan.

buildSteps.title: Test at scale
buildSteps.detail: Run tens to hundreds of units in the lab, then thousands of very simple ones to check that self-assembly still works as numbers grow.

buildSteps.title: Add real work capability
buildSteps.detail: Give an assembled structure the strength, sensors and control to lift, carry or manipulate something useful — mostly still a research goal.

buildSteps.title: Layer on the general-intelligence layer
buildSteps.detail: Train controllers that take an arbitrary task in an unstructured setting and choose a configuration for it. No such system exists today; this step is a research programme, not an engineering task.

prerequisites.why: labs have demonstrated cubes and swarms that link and reshape, but only at small scale and light loads.
thousands of simple robots have self-assembled into shapes in controlled lab conditions.
the force a module can apply at a joint limits what an assembled structure can ever lift.
power has to flow through connected modules, or every unit must carry enough battery for the whole job.
nothing today can look at an unfamiliar physical task and decide how to reshape a robot swarm to do it.
joints must survive millions of connect and release cycles in dirt, water and vibration; no field-proven design exists.

pathway.milestone: lab swarms of simple modules that self-assemble into predetermined shapes
pathway.unlocks: proof that local rules scale to many units.

pathway.milestone: stronger modules that carry real loads and perform simple manipulation in a workshop
pathway.unlocks: first economically useful reconfigurable tasks, such as inspection or handling in tight spaces.

pathway.milestone: heterogeneous swarms with learned controllers working in unstructured environments
pathway.unlocks: robots that adapt their own shape to a job instead of needing a bespoke machine.
flexible automation without purpose-built hardware — contingent on breakthroughs in embodied AI, actuator power density and durable joints that no current research programme has achieved.
